content.text: review the code in this workspace to see if any PII or Sensitive data is being exposed to LLM
I’ll trace each path that sends data to an LLM and check what personal or sensitive fields can reach the model, its provider, or related logs.

The live adapter sends the full message body and office policy to the configured endpoint. I’ll check whether there’s evidence of live processing and whether committed artifacts contain personal data beyond the fictional fixtures.

**Yes. In live OpenAI mode, the application sends the full, unredacted access-request message and office policy to the configured model endpoint.** The local database and checked-in extraction results contain only the 21 fictional fixtures, all processed in mock mode. I found no evidence in those records that real access requests were sent.

| Severity | Finding |
|---|---|
| **High** | **Live mode sends more data than the extraction needs.** Requester and manager names, systems, production privileges, access dates, and business purpose all reach the model. Any unrelated PII or pasted credentials in the free-text message also go through. The configured API key is sent in the HTTP authorization header. [intake.py](access_requests/intake.py:9) · [openai_provider.py](access_requests/openai_provider.py:51) |
| **High** | **The destination is configurable without an HTTPS or host allowlist.** `MODEL_ENDPOINT` controls where both the message and the bearer key are sent. A misconfigured endpoint could expose both. [openai_provider.py](access_requests/openai_provider.py:21) |
| **Medium** | **Copies persist in local files and output.** SQLite retains the entire original export. CLI output and snapshots can contain names and exact quotes, and the override-handling path can copy the full message into a quote. The database and current extraction file had mode `0644`, and snapshots default to the repository’s `deliverables/` directory. [store.py](access_requests/store.py:73) · [policy.py](access_requests/policy.py:38) · [__main__.py](access_requests/__main__.py:21) |
| **Medium** | **The committed coding transcript already contains account and user IDs, workspace paths, and raw tool output.** Entire checkpointing is enabled and configured to sync to `origin`, creating another disclosure path if real records are inspected during a coding session. Remote checkpoint contents were outside this review. [session.jsonl](deliverables/session.jsonl:1) · [Entire settings](.entire/settings.json:1) |

The adapter sets `store: false`. OpenAI documents that default API abuse-monitoring logs can still include prompts and responses and are generally retained for up to 30 days. The project’s retention settings were outside this review. [OpenAI API data controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data#data-retention-controls-for-abuse-monitoring)

Before processing real requests, minimize or tokenize the text locally, restrict outbound calls to approved HTTPS endpoints, and keep raw exports and exact quotes in a restricted review store outside Git and coding-agent capture.

I verified the request payload offline with fictional data and a dummy key. All 45 tests passed. No live model call was made and no files were changed.

I’ll add a privacy boundary before the live model call, restrict where requests can go, and move sensitive runtime artifacts out of the repo’s default output path. Then I’ll verify the protections offline.

I’ll use request-local placeholders for names, systems, IDs, dates, and free text. The model will see a limited set of access-request terms, and the app will restore exact evidence locally for reviewers. That keeps the raw message out of both the model request and routine CLI output.
